summary: Multiplexed client handshake merges sessions during canary, causing pinned-version handshake split and automated fallback to degraded variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Novara Health observed a class of requests that had been explicitly pinned to redwood-v2-13b-quant-muted during a staged canary roll that were suddenly served by the fallback variant redwood-v2-13b-fallback. The transition coincided with heavy client-side HTTP/2 multiplexing and a burst of keepalive/reconnects from a downstream proxy.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints returned lower-quality outputs for ~8 minutes for a small cohort (~0.6% of their traffic), causing a product regression and one elevated support alert.
- Observed token-cost increase due to fallback variant having a different batching/quantization profile.
- Customer reporting incorrect inference outputs in clinical summarization tests.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: novara-dedicated-1 (prod-us-east)
- Canary variant: redwood-v2-13b-quant-muted (pinned for cohort via per-tenant policy)
- Edge: client -> customer-proxy -> redwood-edge-proxy (h2 multiplexing enabled) -> api-gateway -> orchestrator -> serving-runtime

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer traffic with persistent connection and HTTP/2 multiplexing active.
2) Large number of concurrent keepalive PINGs and a reconnect wave from customer-proxy at 2026-03-13T16:07:12Z.
3) Orchestrator logs show two session IDs merged for the same tenant during the canary traffic-slice reconciliation window.
4) Pin-handshake trace shows a partial commit (pin_assign -> pin_ack) followed by a separate session completing the request without the pin metadata, which triggered routing policy to pick fallback variant.

Relevant logs / telemetry snippets (sanitized):
- edge-proxy: 2026-03-13T16:07:12Z INFO keepalive burst from 10.12.34.56: 102 concurrent streams
- orchestrator: 2026-03-13T16:07:13Z WARN session-merge detected tenant=novara-h tenant_id=tn-9032 merge_candidate_ids=[s-12121,s-12122]
- orchestrator: 2026-03-13T16:07:13Z DEBUG pin-handshake tenant=tn-9032 stage=assign trace_id=tr-0a1b pin_variant=redwood-v2-13b-quant-muted status=partial_commit
- api-gateway: 2026-03-13T16:07:13Z ERROR routing-fallback tenant=tn-9032 selected_variant=redwood-v2-13b-fallback reason=pin-missing

Investigation notes so far:
- Hypothesis A: HTTP/2 multiplexing plus edge-level session coalescing caused pin metadata to be lost when two streams were combined. The orchestrator currently assumes per-session pin metadata is monotonic and not re-seen across merged streams; merge produces a race.
- Hypothesis B: Keepalive/reconnect wave caused a timing window where the pin_cohort assignment was written to the control-plane snapshot but not yet visible to the edge shard; combined session then routed by local decision to fallback.
- We identified a correlation between a specific edge-proxy middleware change (h2 stream reuse optimization, PR referenced above) and the timing of the first occurrence; rollback of that middleware in a staging environment reproduced a session-merge warning but did not reproduce a pin loss unless we forced a reconnect storm.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Support applied a short-lived sticky-route override for the affected tenant to force explicit variant selection for 30 minutes (manual policy) at 2026-03-13T16:20Z; customer traffic returned to pinned variant.
- Increased observability: enabled trace-level pin-handshake logging for the tenant and edge shard for the next 24 hours.

Open questions and next steps:
1) Reproduce in a controlled staging load test that uses h2 multiplexing + reconnect bursts to confirm the merge->pin-loss path.
2) Determine whether the orchestrator should tag per-request pin tokens (instead of per-session) for safety when session merging is enabled.
3) If root cause is edge stream reuse optimization, plan a targeted fix or a compatibility flag to disable stream coalescing for tenants with pinned rollouts.
4) Run retrospective across other tenants to surface if this was an isolated incident or a systemic risk.

Desired outcome:
- Root cause identified and fix shipped (edge or orchestrator) to prevent pin metadata loss when session merges occur.
- Automated detection rule added to alert on session-merge + pin_partial_commit patterns and immediately throttle pin-sensitive decisions or enforce conservative routing.

2026-03-13T16:23:40Z - Infra (Marcus Liu): Applied tenant sticky-route override. Observed immediate rebind to pinned variant in traces. Enabling debug pin-handshake logs for tenant on edge shard e-us-03.

2026-03-13T18:02:12Z - On-call Orchestrator Eng (Priya Kapoor): Reproduced session-merge warning in staging when running a reconnect storm with multiplexed streams. Pin metadata persisted if we disable stream coalescing. Suspect edge middleware optimization is exposing race. Investigating codepath in orchestrator session-merge handler.

2026-03-14T09:30:00Z - Support (Elena Park): Customer confirmed outputs normalized after override. Novara requests a postmortem and prefer a configuration knob to opt out of stream coalescing for critical tenants.

2026-03-14T11:12:07Z - Infra (Marcus Liu): Next action: create unit + integration test for session-merge with pinned handshakes (owner: orchestrator team). Tentative patch to ensure per-request pin-token is carried in header when merge detected. Planning a canary patch to edge-proxy with disable flag for coalescing.
